title: We Audited 10 Frontier Open AI Models—Here Is Why They All Dropped Expert-Choice Routing!
summary: A two-part technical audit examined the configurations of ten frontier open-weight Mixture-of-Experts models, including DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.6, and Kimi K2, documenting an industry convergence toward auxiliary-loss-free sigmoid gating and shared experts. The report revealed that Expert-Choice Routing remains absent from causal open LLMs because it triggers a 10% abnormal loss drop from causal leakage of future tokens.
raw_text: So check this out—a massive two-part engineering audit just cracked open the Hugging Face config files of ten frontier open-weight Mixture-of-Experts models, including DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.6, Kimi K2, and GLM-4.5. Everyone in the open-source AI community has been wondering why every single one of these labs is converging on the exact same architecture: auxiliary-loss-free sigmoid gating, shared active experts, and crazy sparsity ratios scaling up to 128x. Here's the wild part: on paper, a method called Expert-Choice Routing—where each expert picks its own top tokens—accelerates training convergence by more than 2x. Yet literally zero of the ten open causal LLMs use it! Why? Because DeepSeek researchers discovered that during autoregressive training, Expert-Choice Routing causes a sneaky 10% abnormal loss drop by leaking future tokens into the past! Honestly, this is huge for ML engineers—plus, the audit showed that using dynamic top-k serving in SGLang boosts P99 Time-To-First-Token by up to 1.26x right out of the box!
